topic: Why chatbots miscounted the letters in strawberry: they read tokens (numbered chunks), not letters

through_line.name: the giant strawberry
through_line.progression: the strawberry is pressed into a cube, chopped into chunks, swapped for cubes in drawers, rebuilt from merged chunks, replaced by a row of cubes, and turned whole into a single cube
through_line.resolution: a fresh strawberry rests under the machine's funnel beside one glowing cube, as in the opening

blocks.vo_line: To a chatbot, strawberry can be one number. It helps explain why popular ones once insisted the word has two Rs, when it has three.
blocks.through_line_state: a giant strawberry slams into the machine and is pressed into one glowing cube
shots: CLOSE-UP, static: a giant glossy strawberry drops from above and slams into the machine's funnel with a bang, juice droplets flying
LOW ANGLE WIDE, gentle drift: the whole machine shakes and puffs steam on the factory floor as its press stamps down hard
EXTREME CLOSE-UP, slow push-in: the output chute door snaps open and a single glowing yellow cube pops out
HIGH ANGLE MEDIUM, static: the cube bounces twice along the conveyor belt and skids to a stop
LOW ANGLE CLOSE-UP, static: the cube sits pulsing with light on the belt while steam curls past

blocks.vo_line: Before a chatbot reads anything, software chops your text into chunks called tokens. In English, one token averages about four characters.
blocks.through_line_state: strawberries ride the belt and a blade chops each one into a few chunks
shots: MEDIUM, lateral drift: a row of strawberries rides the conveyor belt toward a big chopping blade
EXTREME CLOSE-UP, static: the blade slams down with a thunk and a strawberry splits into chunks
HIGH ANGLE WIDE, slow crane down: chopped chunks stream along the belt in a long neat line
CLOSE-UP, static: four small chunks slide together and click into one tidy group
LOW ANGLE MEDIUM, slow push-in: the groups of chunks tip off the belt end into a waiting cart one after another

blocks.vo_line: Each chunk becomes an ID number from a fixed list, often a hundred thousand entries or more. So where do the letters go?
blocks.through_line_state: each strawberry chunk is dropped into a drawer and comes back as a plain cube
shots: WIDE, slow push-in: a towering hall of thousands of small drawers, a cart of strawberry chunks rolling in
CLOSE-UP, static: one drawer shoots open with a clack and a strawberry chunk drops inside
LOW ANGLE MEDIUM, gentle drift: drawers pop open and shut in a wave up the wall
EXTREME CLOSE-UP, static: a drawer slides out again holding a plain glowing cube instead of the chunk
HIGH ANGLE MEDIUM, slow orbit: cubes rain down a chute into a tray while the last strawberry chunk vanishes into its drawer

blocks.vo_line: The list is built by counting. Letter pairs seen together most often get merged, over and over, until common words are single chunks.
blocks.through_line_state: strawberry chunks snap together in pairs until one whole strawberry is a single piece
shots: CLOSE-UP, static: two small strawberry chunks slide toward each other on a counter and snap together with a click
HIGH ANGLE WIDE, gentle drift: across the hall floor, dozens of chunk pairs snap together in a rippling wave
EXTREME CLOSE-UP, slow push-in: a joined pair snaps onto a third chunk, growing bigger
LOW ANGLE MEDIUM, static: the last piece locks on with a heavy clunk and a whole strawberry stands complete
OVERHEAD CLOSE-UP, static: the whole strawberry drops into a single open drawer that slams shut

blocks.vo_line: So the chatbot only ever works with those numbers, and it writes back the same way: predicting one token at a time.
blocks.through_line_state: no strawberry in sight: the machine pushes out one cube at a time into a growing row
shots: LOW ANGLE CLOSE-UP, static: the machine's chute door flips open and one glowing cube shoots out
WIDE LATERAL, gentle drift: a row of cubes grows along the belt, each new cube landing after the last
EXTREME CLOSE-UP, static: a cube lands and clacks tight against its neighbour
HIGH ANGLE MEDIUM, slow push-in: the machine pauses, rattles, then pops out exactly one more cube
MEDIUM, slow orbit: the long line of cubes glides away down the belt past a lone strawberry stalk left on the floor

blocks.vo_line: Here is where the letters went. Inside a sentence, one popular tokenizer turns strawberry into a single ID: no letters, only a number.
blocks.through_line_state: a whole strawberry goes into one drawer and comes out as one cube with nothing inside
shots: MEDIUM, static: a whole strawberry rolls along the counter and hops into one open drawer
EXTREME CLOSE-UP, static: the drawer slams shut with a bang and its handle glows
LOW ANGLE WIDE, slow crane up: the wall of drawers lights up in a ripple spreading from that one drawer
CLOSE-UP, slow push-in: the drawer slides open and a single glowing cube rises out, no strawberry left
OVERHEAD MEDIUM, static: the cube splits open in two halves, showing it is solid and empty of seeds or fruit

blocks.vo_line: The model has to learn spelling from patterns in its training text, not by looking. Which sounds impossible once you remember that
blocks.through_line_state: the cube and a fresh strawberry sit side by side at the machine, back where it began
shots: HIGH ANGLE CLOSE-UP, static: hundreds of glowing cubes pour through the machine's funnel in a rattling stream
MEDIUM LATERAL, gentle drift: the machine hums and lays cubes down in a neat row along the belt
EXTREME CLOSE-UP, static: one cube taps a fresh strawberry resting on the belt with a soft clink
LOW ANGLE WIDE, slow crane up: the belt carries the cube and the strawberry side by side through the bright factory
CLOSE-UP, slow push-in: the strawberry settles under the machine's funnel, the cube glowing calmly beside it
